messages.content: I’m ready to settle Amelia Island. Before I book, verify exactly what the king rooms mean by balcony and ocean view at both hotels. I don’t want to pay for wording that only means the hotel is near the water.

For September 12 through 18, I found one relevant king category at each finalist. At Omni, the Ocean View King guarantees an Atlantic-facing view from the room and has a small private furnished balcony with two chairs. It is not the resort-view king from the earlier quote. At SpringHill, the King Suite with Balcony has a larger private balcony, but the listed view is partial ocean view; buildings and vegetation may interrupt it. Neither listing describes the SpringHill room as direct oceanfront.
And the standard king at Omni that we priced before has no balcony or ocean view, correct?

Correct. The $3,295.68 Omni quote was for a Resort View King. Its outlook can face the grounds or parking area, and that category does not guarantee a balcony. The Ocean View King is the category that guarantees both the water-facing outlook and the small private balcony.
Give me the final refundable totals for the two rooms you just described, including every required charge and parking.

Omni Ocean View King: $3,874.56 for six nights, including room tax, the daily resort fee, and self-parking. A refundable two-night deposit of $1,196.32 is charged at booking and counts toward that total. SpringHill King Suite with Balcony and partial ocean view: $2,328.12 total, including taxes; breakfast and self-parking are included, and there is no resort fee. Both quotes are for one room and two adults.
Now compare the refund dates carefully. One of them tightened up earlier.

The Omni rate can be canceled without penalty through 5:00 p.m. local hotel time on September 5. After that, the two-night deposit of $1,196.32 becomes the cancellation penalty. The SpringHill rate remains fully refundable through 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on September 10; after that, the stated penalty is one night, currently $372.18 including tax. Changes can trigger repricing at either property.
So SpringHill gives us the bigger balcony and more time to cancel, but it’s across the road and the water view is only partial.

That’s right. SpringHill is $1,546.44 less, has the larger balcony, and gives you five additional days before its cancellation cutoff. Its beach route still uses the marked Atlantic Avenue crossing and Main Beach boardwalk. Omni costs more and locks in sooner, but the room guarantees an Atlantic-facing view and the hotel’s path reaches its beach boardwalk without a public-road crossing.
Does Omni’s small balcony actually have room for both of us to sit, or is it one of those standing ledges?

It is described as a furnished private balcony, not a standing ledge. The room details specify seating for two, though the published photos show a compact depth with the chairs positioned close to the railing. The view is labeled ocean view rather than oceanfront, so the angle can vary within the category, but the Atlantic must be visible.
All right. Book the Omni Ocean View King for all six nights. One room for Avery Thompson and Morgan Thompson. Use the refundable rate, not any advance-purchase offer.

Before I submit it: the refundable total is $3,874.56, with $1,196.32 charged now as a two-night deposit. Free cancellation ends at 5:00 p.m. local time September 5, after which that deposit is the penalty. The reservation will be September 12 through 18 for two adults in one Ocean View King with a private balcony. Shall I place it using the payment method ending in 1842?
Yes. Use the card ending 1842 and book it under Avery Thompson. Morgan should be listed as the second guest.

The Omni Amelia Island Resort is booked for September 12 through 18 under Avery Thompson, with Morgan Thompson listed as the second guest. Confirmation: OAI-746291. The reserved category is one Ocean View King with a private furnished balcony for two adults. The six-night total is $3,874.56 including taxes, resort fees, and self-parking; the $1,196.32 refundable deposit was charged to the card ending 1842. Cancellation is free through 5:00 p.m. local hotel time September 5, after which the deposit becomes the penalty. SpringHill remains unbooked.
